title: scheduler-trace-fusion-and-heuristic-manifest
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This document defines the Scheduler Trace Fusion (STF) design and the operational heuristic manifest that ties runtime scheduler decisions to rich trace telemetry. The goal is to enable data-driven scheduler heuristics that are auditable, testable, and safe to roll out in production across hosted, dedicated and private deployments.

Audience

- Runtime engineers implementing scheduling policies
- Profiling and observability engineers creating telemetry contracts
- On-call and SRE teams validating rollouts and diagnosing regressions

Motivation

Current scheduler decisions are driven by lightweight counters and tokenized signals (queue length, slot availability, priority). That design is fast but opaque: root cause of latency spikes and harmful fairness regressions is often lost. By fusing per-request traces with scheduler decision telemetry we can:

- Recover causal relationships between kernel selection and latency outcomes
- Automatically detect heuristic regressions during canaries and can trigger safe rollback
- Build feature-rich heuristics that use historical traces to adapt admission and batching policies

Goals and Non-Goals

Goals:
- Define a minimal trace->scheduler contract that is cheap to collect and rich enough for offline inference and online heuristics.
- Provide a library of vetted heuristics and a safe rollout/rollback playbook.
- Ensure auditable experiment data for quality/regression alerts.

Non-Goals:
- This doc does not replace kernel-level profiling (use kernel-profiling playbooks for low-level GPU traces).
- This is not a capacity-planning manual; it focuses on decision signals and observability.

Key Concepts

1) Trace Fusion: attach a light-weight "scheduling-context" envelope to each request trace that records the scheduler's inputs and outputs at decision time. The envelope is stored as a 1) local runtime annotation and 2) sampled telemetry sent to the observability pipeline.

2) Heuristic Manifest: a canonical registry of scheduling heuristics. Each heuristic includes: id, inputs, expected outputs, safety checks, and metrics to validate.

3) Fairness Window: a sliding time window (default 5m) where per-tenant resource shares are enforced. Heuristics must declare expected fairness impact.

4) Backpressure Signals: boolean and scalar signals emitted by kernel-dispatcher and gpu-pool-manager used by heuristics (e.g., slot_throttle_pct, kvcache_warmness).

Telemetry & Data Contract

The runtime must emit the following fields (pipe-separated table below for quick copy/paste):

| field | type | description | sampling strategy | example |
|-------|------|-------------|-------------------|---------|
| trace_id | string | global trace identifier | always | t_6d8f... |
| timestamp_utc | iso8601 | request decision timestamp | always | 2026-07-28T12:03:05Z |
| tenant_id | string | customer or internal tenant id | always | acme-corp |
| route | string | API route or model route | always | /v1/complete |
| scheduler_decision | string | chosen path (keep, preempt, piggyback, evict) | always | piggyback |
| kernel_hint | string | kernel/quantization variant suggested | sampled (1%) | q8hf32 |
| queue_depth | int | local queue depth at decision | always | 12 |
| slot_util_pct | float | percent of logical slots occupied | always | 76.3 |
| kvcache_hit_pct | float | recent kvcache prefix hit rate | sampled (10%) | 87.5 |
| latency_observed_ms | float | final end-to-end latency if available | sampled | 258.1 |
| decision_notes | string | optional free-form why the decision was made | sampled | "priority=high, slot_reuse" |

Sampling guidance:
- "always" fields are inexpensive and should be produced for every request.
- Kernel/quantization hints and full latency outcome can be sampled (1-10%) to reduce ingestion cost. Sampling stratified by route and tenant.

Scheduler Integration Points

The following runtime components must be updated to support STF:

- runtime-scheduler: attach scheduling-context to requests prior to kernel selection.
- kernel-dispatcher: emit backpressure signals and record kernel_hint chosen.
- request-proxy: propagate trace_id and lightweight annotations across service boundaries.
- observability-ingestor: accept STF payloads and store into the tracing index (schema above).

Heuristics Library (v1)

Each heuristic entry below is short and must be accompanied by unit tests and a canary plan.

1) adaptive-burst-fuse
- intent: fuse small bursty requests from same tenant into a single batch up to N ms (default 3 ms) to improve throughput.
- inputs: queue_depth, tenant_burst_rate_1m, slot_util_pct
- expected outcome: +10-30% throughput for elastic tenants, <5% latency increase for p50 p95
- safety checks: stop if p95 latency regression > 15% for any route in canary.

2) fairness-compensation
- intent: temporarily lower batch sizes for tenants that exceeded their fairness budget in the Fairness Window.
- inputs: fairness_window_violation_count, tenant_share_pct
- expected outcome: enforce long-term fairness while avoiding immediate outages
- safety checks: ensure no tenant sees p50 > 300ms

3) kvcache-warmth-aware-routing
- intent: prefer routes/slots with higher kvcache_hit_pct to improve tail latency for chat workloads.
- inputs: kvcache_hit_pct, route, model_variant
- expected outcome: lower p95 and tail-cost per token
- safety checks: metrics must be validated by shadow runs before active routing change.

Runtime Configuration Examples

Below is a sample declarative snippet used by runtime-scheduler to register heuristics (YAML):

```yaml
heuristics:
  - id: adaptive-burst-fuse
    enabled: true
    params:
      max_fuse_ms: 3
      tenant_threshold_rps: 50
    safety_checks:
      p95_latency_pct_increase_threshold: 15
      canary_sampling: 5
  - id: fairness-compensation
    enabled: false
    params:
      fairness_window_mins: 5
      min_batch_size: 1
```

Operational Playbook: Deploying a New Heuristic

1) Author and unit-test the heuristic locally and in unit benchmark harness.
2) Run offline replay against the synthetic workload corpus (see benchmarking suite). Validate metrics vs baseline.
3) Create a canary release: enable the heuristic with canary_sampling 5% and safety_checks enabled.
4) Run an automated validation pipeline for 1h with the following checks:
   - p50 and p95 latency deviation < 10% across routes
   - request error rate delta < 0.05%
   - tenant fairness delta within expected bounds
5) If validation passes, ramp to 25% for 4h, then full rollout using incremental steps (25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 30m observations at each step.
6) If at any point safety checks fail, automated rollback to previous heuristic configuration and open P1 incident.

Emergency Mitigation Procedures

1) Failure mode detection: an STF safety alert fires if p95 latency increases > 20% or global error rate increases > 0.5% in 10 minutes.
2) Immediate steps:
   a) Disable heuristics via runtime feature-flag (FAST_BUTTON) for all active nodes.
   b) Switch runtime-scheduler to "conservative" policy (batch_size=1, no piggyback).
   c) Notify on-call via pager and attach the latest STF trace dump to the incident.
3) Recovery: monitor 15m trend; if stable, re-enable heuristics in canary for 10% then ramp.

Profiling Experiments to Validate Heuristics

- Baseline replay: replay the production request corpus for 24h and record STF telemetry.
- Shadow routing experiment: run heuristic in shadow (no decision effect) for at least 6h. Compare predicted outcome against actual.
- Synthetic stress test: create synthetic microbursts and long-tail chat sessions; validate fairness and tail-latency.

Benchmarking Metrics and Targets

- p50 latency baseline per route (ms): capture and store in benchmark manifest.
- p95 latency regression threshold: < +10% for canary, < +5% for final rollout.
- throughput uplift: target 10-25% for adaptive-burst-fuse on elastic workloads.
- fairness adherence: tenant share deviation < 5% over a 24h window.

Runbook Snippets and CLI

- To dump recent STF traces for a tenant:
  kubectl exec -n runtime-svc runtime-scheduler-xxx -- /bin/stf-cli dump --tenant acme-corp --since 30m > /tmp/acme-stf.json

- To toggle heuristic:
  stfctl set heuristic adaptive-burst-fuse --enabled=false --cluster all

Rollout Checklist

- [ ] Unit tests & regressions in CI
- [ ] Offline replay passes (no regressions)
- [ ] Canary configuration with safety_checks defined
- [ ] Alerting rules deployed that reference STF telemetry fields
- [ ] Dashboard & runbook updated with links to trace queries

Ownership and SLAs

- Owner: runtime-scheduler team (primary)
- SRE liaison: oncall-runtime@redwood.ai
- SLAs relevant to STF rollouts: p95 latency SLO for API routes (default: 300ms), error-rate SLO 0.5%

Related Pages and Artifacts

- profiling-playbook: causal-latency-attribution (for enrichment methods)
- kernel-and-scheduling: predictive-slotting-orchestration (for capacity knobs)
- benchmarking suite: replay corpus locations and synthetic builders

Appendix: Minimal Trace Query Examples

- Find all traces where a fairness-compensation decision was applied in the last hour and p95 > 200ms:
  trace_index.query("scheduler_decision=\"fairness-compensation\" AND timestamp > now()-1h") | filter(p95 > 200)

Glossary

- scheduler_decision: the action the scheduler took for a request prior to kernel dispatch.
- kernel_hint: an advisory kernel/variant suggestion attached to the trace.
- fairness_window: timeframe across which tenant shares are measured.

Appendix: Implementation Notes

- Keep scheduling-context small: target < 256 bytes per request for always-emitted fields.
- Use stratified sampling by route and tenant to ensure minority tenants appear in traces.
- Persist fusion-enriched traces for 7 days at high-fidelity, then aggregate metrics for 90 days.

If you are implementing STF, coordinate with observability and SRE before the first canary. Add the heuristic to the manifest registry and attach a minimal test plan to the code change.

End of document.
